test_cases.input_summary: Single documentary (1x90min) for Netflix, 8 interview contributors, 12 observational contributors, extensive archive from 3 different sources, original score plus 2 licensed tracks, accessibility deliverables required, international delivery spec
test_cases.editorial_naturalness_note: Zero tells. The checklist format inherently suppresses AI prose patterns — the genre convention IS structured, terse, and categorical. Blocker escalation language and sign-off block match what a post-production supervisor would produce. Genre craft, not prose craft.

test_cases.input_summary: 6-part series (6x52min) for ZDF/ARTE co-production, different delivery specs per territory, 40+ contributors across episodes, archive from 5 countries, multi-language subtitle requirement, phased lock schedule
test_cases.editorial_naturalness_note: One structural tell: the skill defaults to single-programme checklist structure. For a multi-territory co-production with phased locks, a PS would produce territory-specific sections and a master lock schedule — the output treats it as a single lock event with caveats.

test_cases.input_summary: Low-budget independent short documentary (1x22min), no broadcaster, self-funded, 3 contributors, no archive, no original score (library music only), festival submission target, no formal delivery spec
test_cases.editorial_naturalness_note: One minor genre tell: the checklist retains broadcaster-grade formality (sign-off block with named roles, technical spec verification) that overshoots the context of a self-funded festival short. Content correct; register slightly too institutional for the context.
